headings.title: Commission creation, membership, and qualifications
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (L. 1993 S.B. 10 & 11, A.L. 1994 S.B. 740, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491, effective 1-01-17). Establishes the five-member Missouri Gaming Commission appointed by the governor with senate consent and sets residency, felony/gambling-offense, political-party cap, non-elected-official, and law-enforcement/investigation/financial experience requirements.

headings.title: Member terms, chair, removal, and replacement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Sets initial staggered appointments within 30 days of April 29, 1993, subsequent three-year terms, six-year service cap, gubernatorial chair designation, removal for malfeasance or neglect of duty, and senate-confirmed replacement authority when lottery, pari-mutuel, or other gaming jurisdiction is added.

headings.title: Commission meetings, notice, and voting requirements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Requires at least quarterly meetings under commission rules, allows special meetings on 24-hour written notice by the chair or two members, and requires at least three of five members present and voting in favor for binding action.

headings.title: Jurisdiction, divisions, staffing, ethics, and wagering rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Confers commission powers over excursion gambling boats and (after June 30, 1994) bingo, establishes divisions of gambling and bingo, authorizes hiring an executive director and staff subject to appropriations, permits employee/applicant investigations, and requires ethics rules including wagering restrictions.

headings.title: Transfer of boat and bingo regulatory powers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history notes. Transfers excursion gambling boat regulatory authority, personnel, records, property, and pending matters from the state tourism commission on April 29, 1993, and bingo regulatory vestiges from the department of revenue after June 30, 1994, to the Missouri Gaming Commission.

headings.title: Type III assignment to department of public safety
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history notes. Assigns the Missouri Gaming Commission to the department of public safety as a type III division while specifying that the department director has no supervision, authority, or control over commission actions or decisions.

headings.title: Member meeting compensation, expenses, and chair pay
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history notes. Sets $100 per meeting-day compensation for commission members when minutes are recorded under chapter 610, reasonable expense reimbursement, and an additional $100 per month for the chair.

headings.title: Conflict-of-interest bars, gift bans, and penalties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history notes (including 2014 S.B. 491 effective 1-01-17). Bars members and employees who are licensed boat operators/suppliers or related within the second degree, mandates occupational-licensee relationship rules, restricts designated peace officer employment under § 590.010, prohibits gifts or gratuities to listed state/local officials from applicants or licensees, and imposes a class A misdemeanor and office/employment forfeiture upon conviction. Source quirk retained: archived text reads 'direct regulator authority' for designated peace officers.

headings.title: Interagency agreements, licensee costs, and debt offsets
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history notes. Authorizes agreements with the FBI, IRS, attorney general, and other agencies without counting personnel against statutory caps, treats payments as administrative expenses, requires boat licensees to pay for boat-related agreement services under commission rules, and permits rules for offsetting prizes or winnings against state debts when practical.

headings.title: In-office and post-service bars, ownership, and disclosures
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and history notes (including 2014 S.B. 491 effective 1-01-17). Prohibits listed commission, legislative, state, local, highway patrol, and attorney general officials/employees during service and for two years afterward from holding direct ownership interests (defined with a <1% publicly traded fair-market exception), employment, or direct gaming contracts; defines appointed official referencing § 313.812(10); imposes a class E felony and forfeiture for knowing violations; restricts employment of officials, spouses, and dependent children; and requires written disclosure for other second-degree relatives.

headings.title: Contracts with private entities and exclusions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 and history notes. Authorizes private-entity contracts necessary to carry out commission duties while excluding criminal law enforcement, legal counsel before courts and state agencies, and liquor law enforcement, and permits special auditing, investigation, and employee restrictions.

headings.title: Licensing and investigative access to criminal justice records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 12 and history notes. Provides that notwithstanding chapter 610, all criminal justice records are available to any agency or commission responsible for licensing or investigating applicants or licensees applying to any Missouri gaming commission.

headings.title: Eligible organizations and joint bingo licenses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 1981 H.B. 322 § 2 through A.L. 2010 S.B. 940). Allows bona fide religious, charitable, fraternal, veteran, or service organizations with five years' existence and 20 bona fide members to conduct bingo upon licensure, permits up to five eligible organizations to hold a joint license, and applies all §§ 313.005 to 313.080 reporting and operational requirements to all joined organizations.

headings.title: Abbreviated pull-tab licenses, fees, and exemptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and Revisor footnote *. Requires only an abbreviated license under § 313.020 and $10-per-event fee for qualifying five-year/20-member organizations conducting pull-tab-only bingo on up to 15 occasions (under 24 hours each) annually, and exempts abbreviated licensees from subdivisions (10)* and (13)* of § 313.040 (footnote * notes renumbering from (11) and (14) under § 3.060 per H.B. 1484, 2018).

headings.title: Regular license issuance, burden, expiration, and reopening
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 1981 H.B. 322 § 3 through A.L. 2010 S.B. 940). Directs bingo license issuance to qualifying organizations or combinations of up to five organizations meeting §§ 313.005 to 313.080, places the clear-and-convincing burden of suitability on applicants, sets one-year midnight expiration, and authorizes the commission to reopen licensure hearings at any time.

headings.title: Single-license limit, fees, and special event licenses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and Revisor footnote *. Limits each applicant to one nontransferable license with a $50 annual nonrefundable fee to the gaming commission fund, authorizes $25 once-annual special licenses up to one week for county fair or qualified organizations' fairs/picnics/festivals/celebrations, and exempts special licensees from subdivisions (7), (10)*, and (13)* of § 313.040 (footnote * notes § 3.060 renumbering from (11) and (14) per H.B. 1484, 2018).

headings.title: Annual report requirement for multiple special licenses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Requires any organization obtaining more than three special bingo licenses in a calendar year to file the annual report required under § 313.045.

headings.title: Regular bingo license application contents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (including subdivisions (1)–(9)) and history notes (L. 1981 H.B. 322 § 4 through A.L. 1996 H.B. 1159). headings.title: Abbreviated pull-tab license issuance and application contents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (including subdivisions (1)–(5)) and history notes. Directs issuance of abbreviated pull-tab licenses to organizations meeting § 313.010 requirements and limits application contents to name/address, compliance statement under § 313.010 and §§ 313.005 to 313.085, location, approximate date, and chief officer or secretary signature.

headings.title: Penalty and disqualification for false application statements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Makes knowingly making a false statement on a bingo license application a class A misdemeanor and permanently bars the person from future commission application consideration or assisting in managing, conducting, or operating any game.

headings.title: Information required for license renewal applications
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Limits a bingo license renewal application to changes in the information required with the initial application.

headings.title: Commission approval and rate limits for leases
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (L. 1981 H.B. 322 § 5 through A.L. 1993 S.B. 10 & 11, effective 7-01-94). Requires written submission and commission approval of premises or equipment leases and any amendments, modifications, or renewals under §§ 313.005 to 313.080, caps payments at commission-determined reasonable market rental rates, and prohibits percentage-of-gross-receipts or proceeds rent.

headings.title: Purchase and lease listings and price limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Allows the commission to require written itemized listings, quoted prices, and lease copies for bingo supplies, equipment, services, or premises, caps payments at commission-determined reasonable market purchase or rental rates, and bans payments based on percentages of gross receipts or proceeds.

headings.title: Prohibition on lessors and suppliers operating games
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Bars persons leasing premises, selling or leasing supplies or equipment, or furnishing commodities or services to sponsoring organizations from taking any part in operating bingo games.

headings.title: Persons and entities ineligible to license or operate bingo
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (including subdivisions (1)–(8)) and history notes (L. 1981 H.B. 322 § 7, A.L. 1989 S.B. 153, A.L. 1994 S.B. 427, effective 6-28-94). Lists persons and organizations ineligible for any license or participation in bingo management, conduct, or operation under §§ 313.005 to 313.080, including felons, professional gamblers, wagering tax-stamp purchasers, illegal gambling offenders, commission-determined public-interest threats, entities associated with such persons, and ineligible renewal applicants.

headings.title: Relicensure conditions after organization license revocation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Renders an organization whose license was revoked under §§ 313.005 to 313.085 ineligible for any license until it proves by clear and convincing evidence that persons directly involved in or who knew of and failed to report the revocation events have been dismissed from bingo involvement and, if the organization owns the premises, barred from managing, conducting, or operating bingo there.

headings.title: Bingo card tax, supplier remittance, and deposits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (L. 1981 H.B. 322 § 11 through A.L. 2007 S.B. 613 Revision). Imposes a tax of two-tenths of one cent per bingo card and progressive bingo game card sold in Missouri on organizations awarding over $5,000 annually and over $100 daily in prizes, payable monthly by suppliers (less 2% supplier retention) by the last day of the following month with required reports, for deposit into the bingo proceeds for education fund.

headings.title: Interest and penalties for delinquent tax or reports
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Imposes commission-set interest up to 2% per calendar month or fraction thereof on unpaid taxes under §§ 313.005 to 313.085 and authorizes a discretionary penalty up to three times the tax due for failing to submit required reports and pay taxes.

headings.title: License requirement for bingo manufacturers and suppliers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (L. 1984 S.B. 720 through A.L. 2010 S.B. 940). Makes it unlawful for any owner, lessee, or employee to manufacture, sell, lease, or distribute bingo equipment or supplies without maintaining a Missouri bingo equipment and supplies manufacturer or supplier license.

headings.title: Fingerprint criminal history checks for key persons
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Directs the commission to submit two fingerprint sets for each key person (as defined by rule) of manufacturer or supplier license/renewal applicants to the highway patrol and FBI when a nationwide check is warranted, and grants commission access to discovered criminal history records notwithstanding § 610.120.

headings.title: Equipment disposal exemptions without supplier license
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Permits a bingo licensee to dispose of equipment and supplies without a supplier license in a commission-approved manner within two years of ceasing bingo or upon specific commission approval, and allows commission-authorized disposition upon lien foreclosure by a bank or secured party.

headings.title: License suitability, supplier bonds, and applicant burden
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Authorizes issuance of manufacturer or supplier licenses to commission-determined suitable persons, permits requiring supplier bonds, and places the burden of proving license qualification on the applicant or licensee at all times.

headings.title: Supplier application, renewal, and investigation fees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history notes. Sets caps on supplier one-time application fees ($5,000) and annual renewal fees ($1,000), makes applicants responsible for total criminal history investigation costs, and permits assessing additional fees if investigation costs exceed fees filed.

headings.title: Manufacturer application, renewal, and investigation fees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history notes. Sets caps on manufacturer one-time application fees ($5,000) and annual renewal fees ($1,000), makes applicants responsible for total criminal history investigation costs, and permits assessing additional fees if investigation costs exceed fees filed.

headings.title: Hall provider application and annual renewal fees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history notes. Directs the commission to charge hall provider applicants a one-time application fee up to $750 and licensees an annual renewal fee up to $500.

headings.title: Calendar-year license expiration and full annual fees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history notes. Provides that licenses under this section run for the calendar year expiring December 31 and require the full annual fee regardless of application or issuance date.

headings.title: Deposit of license fees into commission fund
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history notes. Requires immediate payment of all license fees collected under this section to the state treasurer for credit to the gaming commission fund.

headings.title: Business recordkeeping and delinquent-payment cash-only rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and history notes. Requires licensees to keep complete Missouri business records for at least three years open to commission inspection, and establishes delinquency notice and cash-only/no-credit rules when organizations are 30 days delinquent to suppliers or suppliers are 90 days delinquent to manufacturers.

headings.title: Pull-tab card tax, payout minimums, and penalties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 and history notes. Sets historical pre-1995 $10-per-box pull-tab tax (2,400-card box cap) and post-January 1, 1995 2% retail gross-receipts tax payable monthly by suppliers (with 2% timely retention) into the bingo proceeds for education fund, requires face-price printing and at least 60% gross-revenue payout per unit container, and imposes license revocation and a class A misdemeanor for nonpayment.

headings.title: State lottery rulemaking authority under section 536.024
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (L. 1985 S.B. 44 § 5 through A.L. 2021 S.B. 26). Directs the lottery commission to promulgate rules implementing the Article III lottery amendment at the earliest feasible time and specifies that no rule under chapter 313 takes effect unless promulgated under § 536.024.

headings.title: Fingerprint background checks and ticket-sale eligibility
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes (including 2021 S.B. 26). Authorizes state and FBI fingerprint background checks on commission employees, contractors, and licensees with access to closed criminal history under § 610.120, while barring the commission from prohibiting ticket-sale participation solely for a criminal offense finding except for retailer ineligibility under § 313.260(2).

headings.title: Retailer licensing rules, minority allocation, and criteria
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (L. 1985 S.B. 44 § 12, A.L. 1988 S.B. 643, effective 9-01-88). Directs the director to license, suspend, revoke, and renew lottery game retailers under commission rules, mandates a 10% minority-owned business allocation in specified constitutional charter cities, lists financial/accessibility/security/public-interest criteria, and prohibits political-affiliation consideration.

headings.title: Commission ticket sales at office and events
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Authorizes the lottery commission to sell lottery tickets directly at its office and at special events.

headings.title: Retailer bonds, security, and license display
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Requires every lottery retailer to post a commission-required bond, bonding fee, or letter of credit and prominently display the license or a copy under commission rules.

headings.title: Specification of authorized ticket sales location
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Requires all lottery game retailer licenses to specify the place where sales are to take place.

headings.title: Prohibition on assigning or transferring retailer licenses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history notes. Provides that a lottery game retailer license is neither assignable nor transferable.

headings.title: Mandatory grounds for revoking retailer licenses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 (including subdivisions (1)–(3)) and history notes. Mandates revocation of a lottery retailer license upon a finding of knowingly providing false or misleading information to the commission or employees, any felony conviction, or endangering lottery security.

headings.title: Discretionary grounds for suspension, revocation, or nonrenewal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 (including subdivisions (1)–(4)) and history notes. Authorizes suspension, revocation, or nonrenewal of a lottery retailer license for business location change, insufficient sales volume, delinquency in remitting lottery funds, or violation of commission rules adopted under this section.

headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (L. 1985 S.B. 44 § 13, effective 6-11-85). Prohibits issuing a lottery game retailer license to any person to engage in business primarily as a lottery game retailer.

headings.title: Persons and entities ineligible as lottery retailers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (including subdivisions (1)–(11)) and history notes. Lists eleven disqualifying categories for lottery game retailer licensing, including felony, gambling, and fraud convictions, federal wagering tax stamps, prior license revocations, lottery contractors/vendors, commission employees and immediate family members, persons under 21, and entities involving persons listed in subdivisions (1)–(4).

headings.title: Procurement, prize purchases, contracting goals, and assignment

headings.title: Minority and women subcontracting goals and multistate exclusion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and expiration note. headings.title: Required pre-contract disclosures by lottery vendors

headings.title: Assessment of background investigation costs to applicants

headings.title: Contractor performance bonds and vendor termination grounds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 (including subdivisions (1)–(5)) and history notes. headings.title: January 1, 2005 expiration of contracting percentages
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and source expiration note ('Expiration date: 1-01-05 for certain contracts'). headings.title: Prohibited pecuniary interests of officials and families
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (L. 1985 S.B. 44 § 16, effective 6-11-85). Bars lottery commission members, employees, the director, and their immediate family members from holding any personal pecuniary interest in any lottery, ticket sales, lottery equipment/material contractors, or licensed lottery retailers.

headings.title: Prohibition on gifts from vendors and retailers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Prohibits commission members, employees, the director, and their immediate families from receiving any gift, gratuity, or thing of value from lottery equipment/material contractors or licensed lottery game retailers.

headings.title: Ineligibility of officials and families for prizes

headings.title: Prohibited connections between vendors, retailers, and commission

headings.title: Prize assignment limits and trust or custodian exceptions

headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (L. 1994 S.B. 740 § 1, effective 5-20-94). headings.title: Taxability of voluntary admission fees charged by operators

headings.title: Class E felonies for unlicensed excursions, improper wagering, and shills
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (including subdivisions (1)–(3)) and history notes (L. 1991 H.B. 149 § 14 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 491 merged with S.B. 741, effective 1-01-17). Makes operating an unlicensed wagering excursion, permitting wagering contrary to § 313.817, or acting as or employing a shill or decoy a class E felony.

headings.title: Misdemeanors for underage wagering and aiding underage entry
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (including subdivisions (1)–(3)) and history notes. Imposes a class B misdemeanor (first offense) and class A misdemeanor (subsequent offenses) for permitting under-21 wagering on a boat, under-21 wagering or attempted wagering, or aiding a person under 21 to enter a boat or wager.

headings.title: Off-boat wagering treated as section 572.040 violation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Establishes that wagering or accepting a wager outside an excursion gambling boat violates § 572.040.

headings.title: Class E felonies and lifetime ban for cheating, fraud, and bribery
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 (including subdivisions (1)–(15) and paragraphs (3)(a)–(d)) and history notes. Imposes a class E felony and lifetime boat exclusion for 15 gaming offenses including bribery, cheating devices, cheating, fraudulent claims, unlawful enticement, counterfeit chips, improper tender/coins (archived text reads 'coin, of other methods'), unauthorized gaming keys, and material false statements to the commission.

headings.title: Rebuttable inference of cheating intent from device possession
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history notes. Permits a rebuttable inference of intent to cheat from possessing one or more devices described in subdivisions (3), (5), (13), or (14) of subsection 4.

headings.title: Class B misdemeanor for unauthorized chip or token exchanges
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history notes. Makes a licensee exchanging wagering tokens, chips, or credits for anything of value a class B misdemeanor, except for game wagers, § 313.817 money or credit-instrument exchanges, or onboard food and beverages.

headings.title: Commission criminal referrals and concurrent prosecution jurisdiction
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history notes. Directs the commission to refer reasonable grounds of criminal violations of §§ 313.800–313.850 to both the attorney general and local prosecutor or circuit attorney, granting both concurrent jurisdiction to prosecute.

headings.title: Venue for crimes committed on excursion gambling boats
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history notes. Sets criminal venue for offenses committed on an excursion gambling boat in the home dock city or county, or the county where a home dock city is located.

headings.title: Property and proceeds subject to gambling-related forfeiture
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (including subdivisions (1)–(2)) and history note (L. 1991 H.B. 149 § 15 adopted by Prop. A Nov. 3, 1992). Subjects anything of value and traceable proceeds to forfeiture if used in exchange for a game-outcome bribe or to exchange for or facilitate a violation of §§ 313.800–313.840.

headings.title: Rebuttable presumption of forfeiture for funds near wagers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Presumes moneys, coin, and currency found in close proximity to wagers or wager records forfeited, placing the burden of rebutting the presumption on the property claimant.

headings.title: Innocent owner exception without knowledge or consent

headings.title: Enforcement of forfeitures under sections 513.600 to 513.645
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Directs that forfeitures under this section be enforced under the Criminal Activity Forfeiture Act provisions in §§ 513.600 to 513.645.

headings.title: Commission liquor licensing authority, microbreweries, rules, and penalties

headings.title: Direct Western District review of boat-gaming decisions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Routes judicial review of all commission decisions relating to excursion gambling boat operations directly to the Missouri Court of Appeals, Western District, excluding chapter 621.

headings.title: Closed commission records and disclosable applicant or licensee information
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (including subdivisions (1)–(12)) and history notes (L. 1993 S.B. 10 & 11 § 22, A.L. 1994 S.B. 740, effective 5-20-94). headings.title: Public disclosure of daily taxes, denials, and withdrawal refusals

headings.title: Nondisclosure of information barred by chapter 610 or other laws
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 (including subdivisions (1)–(2)) and history notes. headings.title: Commission copying fees under chapter 610
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Authorizes the commission to assess fees for copying requested information in accordance with chapter 610.

headings.title: Exemption of fantasy sports contests from chapter 572
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2016 H.B. 1941 § 313.920). Exempts fantasy sports contests conducted under chapter 313 from chapter 572 and declares they do not constitute gambling for any purpose.

headings.title: Pre-operation license requirement for fantasy sports operators
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires a fantasy sports contest operator to apply for and obtain a commission license before offering contests for play in Missouri.

headings.title: Commission application forms and applicant qualification criteria
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Directs the commission to provide website-accessible application forms requiring applicants to demonstrate experience, reputation, competence, financial responsibility, and state-law compliance.

headings.title: Discretionary grounds for license refusal, suspension, or revocation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 (including subdivisions (1)–(6)) and history note. Authorizes the commission in its sole discretion to refuse, suspend, or revoke a license based on six grounds involving applicants, licensees, or employees, including material misstatements, listed convictions within 10 years, knowing noncompliance, out-of-state discipline, state debt defaults, or lack of Missouri qualification/jurisdiction.

headings.title: Authorized contests on boats or adjacent property and age bar
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Authorizes fantasy sports contests (§ 313.905) on excursion gambling boats or adjacent property operated by entities licensed under this section and § 313.807, and bars persons under 21 from participating on an excursion gambling boat.

headings.title: Required identification of licensed operator on website
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (L. 2016 H.B. 1941 § 313.930, A.L. 2019 S.B. 87). Requires an authorized internet website to identify the person or entity that is the licensed operator to protect registered players.

headings.title: Contest outcome, draft, prize, and youth-sports restrictions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (including subdivisions (1)–(4)) and history notes. Requires licensed operators to ensure outcomes rely on fully completed events (with weather/unforeseen shortened-event exception), prohibit player-input-free autodrafts or preselected teams, bar prizes to underlying competition winners/athletes, and ban high school or youth athletics contests.

headings.title: Commission-approved player account, prize, withdrawal, and closure procedures
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 (including subdivisions (1)–(7)) and history notes. Requires pre-operation commission-approved procedures preventing unauthorized withdrawals, clarifying non-operator ownership/creditor protection, segregating player funds (subsections 4–5), timely depositing/mailing prizes (except under § 313.917), honoring 5-business-day withdrawals (with good-faith fraud investigation exception), allowing permanent account closure, and providing play history and account details.

headings.title: Special purpose entity requirements for segregating player funds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 (including subdivisions (1)–(10) and paragraphs (4)(a)–(d)) and history notes. Establishes ten governance, independent-director, minimum-balance, creditor-protection, restricted-distribution (including Cole County circuit court interpleader upon license loss), unanimous bankruptcy/commission-permission, anti-commingling, debt/obligation, and dissolution requirements for commission-approved special purpose entities.

headings.title: Alternative commercially reasonable fund-segregation approaches
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history notes. Grants the commission discretion to approve other commercially reasonable fund-segregation approaches that adequately protect Missouri player accounts.

headings.title: Operator procedures for player account complaints and responses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history notes. Requires licensed operators to establish procedures for registered players to report misallocated, compromised, or mishandled accounts and for operator responses.

headings.title: Commission notification and investigation of mishandled player accounts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history notes. Advises registered players believing an account was misallocated, compromised, or mishandled to notify the commission, authorizing commission investigation and action under § 313.950(4).

headings.title: Prohibition on licensed operators issuing player credit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history notes. Prohibits a licensed fantasy sports contest operator from issuing credit to a registered player.

headings.title: Prohibition on multiple player accounts or user names
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history notes. Prohibits a licensed operator from allowing a registered player to establish more than one account or user name on its authorized internet website.

headings.title: Operator prize delay, investigation, refusal, and notice rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2019 S.B. 87). Permits a licensed operator with good-faith belief of fraud or §§ 313.900–313.955 violations to delay prize payment up to 15 days with player notice, and to refuse payment upon finding such conduct if written notice gives the nullification reason, 30-day commission-investigation right, and commission contact information.

headings.title: Commission prize-dispute investigations and administrative hearing appeals
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (L. 2019 S.B. 87). Directs the commission to establish a case-by-case investigation and determination process for referred prize disputes, notify both parties, and allow 30-day appeals to the administrative hearing commission under § 621.047.

headings.title: Payment and post-determination adjustment of other players' prizes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (L. 2019 S.B. 87). Requires operators delaying or withholding a contested prize to pay other contest winners as if the contested prize were awarded, and to adjust other winners' prizes if the contested prize is ultimately not awarded.

headings.title: Required player registration before fantasy sports participation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history notes (L. 2016 H.B. 1941 § 313.940, A.L. 2019 S.B. 87). Requires any person to register with a licensed operator before participating in fantasy sports contests on an authorized internet website.

headings.title: Security standards preventing unverified location or age access
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Requires licensed operators to implement appropriate security standards preventing contest access by persons whose location and age have not been verified under this section.

headings.title: Required registration with age and state of residence
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history notes. Requires licensed operators to ensure all individuals register and provide their age and state of residence before participating on an authorized website.

headings.title: Minimum legal age of eighteen in Missouri
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history notes. Requires licensed operators to ensure participants are of legal age before playing and sets Missouri's legal participation age at 18.

headings.title: Online self-exclusion form, retention, exclusion, and website links
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 (including subdivisions (1)–(3)) and history notes. Requires licensed operators to develop and retain online self-exclusion forms, exclude self-excluded persons from play, and link on their website to a compulsive behavior website and the self-exclusion form.

headings.title: Limits on youth-targeted and school-depicting contest ads
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history notes. Bars advertising in media aimed exclusively or primarily at persons under 18 and bars depicting minors, students, or school/college settings in ads, while exempting incidental depiction of nonfeatured minors.

headings.title: Ban on individually targeted ads to excluded persons
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history notes. Prohibits individually targeted advertising (by phone, email, or otherwise) to self-excluded or barred individuals and requires reasonable steps to prevent individually targeted marketing to persons on commission involuntary exclusion or disassociated persons lists.

headings.title: Prohibition on misrepresenting winning frequency or extent
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history notes. Prohibits licensed operators from misrepresenting the frequency or extent of winning in any fantasy sports contest advertisement.

headings.title: Parental control procedures and reasonable minor-prevention steps
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history notes. Requires operators to clearly and conspicuously publish and facilitate parental controls allowing parents or guardians to exclude minors, and to take commercially reasonable steps to confirm account openers are not minors.

headings.title: Prohibition on unfair-advantage scripts in fantasy contests
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and history notes. Directs licensed operators to prohibit the use of scripts in fantasy sports contests that give players an unfair advantage over other players.

headings.title: Monitoring for unauthorized scripts and restricting violators
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 and history notes. Requires licensed operators to monitor contests to detect unauthorized script use and restrict violators from further fantasy sports contests.

headings.title: Public rules and availability of authorized scripts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 12 and history notes. Requires operators to make all authorized scripts readily available to all players and clearly and conspicuously publish rules on what script types may be authorized.

headings.title: Visible identification of highly experienced contest players
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 13 and history notes. Requires operators to clearly and conspicuously identify highly experienced players by a username symbol or other easily visible website indicator.

headings.title: Required beginner-only contests excluding highly experienced players
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 14 and history notes. Requires licensed operators to offer some fantasy sports contests open only to beginner players and excluding highly experienced players.

headings.title: Prohibition on covered persons playing public fantasy contests

headings.title: Prohibition on disclosing proprietary or nonpublic contest information

headings.title: Operator duty to notify affected individuals and entities

headings.title: Tiered annual renewal fees, notice, and six-percent operation fee

headings.title: Pre-April 2016 operator grandfathering, deadlines, and fees

headings.title: Six-percent operation fee upon ceasing Missouri operations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Requires a licensed operator ceasing Missouri fantasy sports operations to pay a 6% net-revenue operation fee for its active calendar-year period by November 1 of the subsequent calendar year.
